newsitem.title: USA: Wolverine Partners details Frisch's plan.
newsitem.headline: Wolverine Partners details Frisch's plan.

text.p: Wolverine Partners, which owns a 6.5 percent stake in Frisch's Restaurants Inc, on Thursday proposed that a majority of the restaurant chain's board members not have any ties to management at Frisch's.
Last month, the partnership had filed a formal proxy statement seeking to elect its four nominees to the Frisch's board of directors.
In a statement released Thursday, Wolverine's Barry Nussbaum and Jerry Ruyan offered greater detail on ways they believe Frisch's could improve its standing.
Ruyan, who is running for one of the four board seats in next month's election, said outside board management would put shareholders first, giving them a greater return.

"It is inexcusable to me that in the recent past it has been acceptable to report 'bottom of the barrel' earnings without making the changes necessary to remedy the fixable problems," Ruyan said in a statement.

Ruyan and Nussbaum sent a letter to Frisch's shareholders outlining their plan. They also proposed doing away with the staggered board system, whereby director terms are staggered, preventing shareholders from electing a board all at once.
The annual meeting of the Cincinnati-based Frisch's is to be held on October 7 in Covington, Ky.
Wolverine Partners owns 6.5 percent of Frisch's stock, or 443,600 shares of common stock.
Besides Ruyan and Nussbaum, the other Wolverine Partners representatives seeking spots on the board are Thomas Doan and Arthur Engel.
